cnica.MIOptimizer#

class cnica.MIOptimizer(params=(True, True, False), max_outer_loop_iters=10, max_inner_loop_iters=1000, max_line_search_iters=50, tol=1e-14, gamma=0.02, initial_lr=0.1, filter_half_order=10, filter_max_lag=10, lam=10.0, sparsity_gate_threshold=0.5)[source][source]#

Bases: object

Riemannian Manifold Optimizer using Interior Point (Log-Barrier) methods.

This class minimizes a composite objective function on the manifold of invertible matrices. It is designed to find an optimal linear transformation \(M\) that decorrelates signal components while strictly satisfying non-negativity constraints via log-barrier penalties.

The objective function is defined as:

\[f(M) = f_{\text{main}}(M) + \mu (h_R(M) + h_L(M))\]

where \(f_{\text{main}}\) is the log-determinant of transformed covariances, and \(h_R, h_L\) are the barrier functions for the constraints \(MS > 0\) and \(M^{-T}C > 0\) respectively.

Parameters:

  • params (tuple) – Three flags (use_0th, use_1st, use_2nd) selecting which derivative orders to include in the decorrelation objective. At least one must be True.

  • max_outer_loop_iters (int, default 10) – Number of iterations for the barrier cooling schedule. In each outer iteration, the barrier parameter \(\mu\) is reduced.

  • max_inner_loop_iters (int, default 1000) – Maximum number of descent steps to take for a fixed value of \(\mu\).

  • max_line_search_iters (int, default 50) – Maximum number of backtracking steps to perform during the line search to satisfy the Armijo condition.

  • tol (float, default 1e-12) – Convergence tolerance for the norm of the projected gradient.

  • gamma (float, default 0.02) – The fraction of lowest-magnitude points to prune from the dataset to avoid numerical issues near the origin when enforcing the barrier constraints. The removed points are those with the minimum of either the percentile threshold or the max magnitude threshold.

  • initial_lr (float, default 0.1) – The initial step size (learning rate) for the backtracking line search.

  • filter_half_order (int, default 10) – Half-order \(m\) of the Parks-McClellan FIR filters used to compute 1st and 2nd order temporal derivatives of the input signals.

  • filter_max_lag (int, default 10) – Maximum autocorrelation lag for unsupervised MSRAC-based filter tuning.

  • lam (float, default 10.0) – Regularization strength for the sparsity norm. Set to 0 to disable.

  • sparsity_gate_threshold (float, default 0.5) – Midpoint of the sigmoid gate in the sparsity norm. Rows with a Hoyer density below this value are penalized; rows above it (e.g. dense sine-like signals) are protected.

Notes

Three key numerical techniques keep the optimizer efficient and stable:

1. Boundary Reduction: Barrier constraints are enforced only on the convex hull vertices of C and S (or a support-function approximation for d > 5), reducing barrier terms from O(samples) to O(vertices).

2. Tangent Space Projection: The Euclidean gradient is projected onto the tangent space of SL(n) via

\[Z = \nabla f - \frac{\operatorname{Tr}(M^{-1} \nabla f)}{n} \cdot M\]

keeping \(\det(M)\) stable throughout.

3. Two-Phase Line Search: Backtracking first uses a cheap first-order inverse approximation

\[(M - \alpha Z)^{-1} \approx M^{-1} + \alpha M^{-1} Z M^{-1}\]

to find a candidate step size, then confirms with the exact matrix exponential retraction.

Examples

>>> opt = MIOptimizer(params=(True, True, False), tol=1e-10)
>>> result = opt.fit_transform(C_data, S_data)
>>> optimal_M = result.x

Dunder Methods

static main(M, Sigmas, compute_grad=True)[source][source]#

Decorrelation objective: sum of log diagonal variances of transformed covariances.

For each covariance \(\Sigma\) in Sigmas (one per active derivative order), computes:

\[f_{\text{main}}(M) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{\Sigma} \sum_{i} \log\left([M \Sigma M^T]_{ii} + \epsilon\right)\]

Minimizing this drives \(M\) toward a transformation where each output channel has low variance across all derivative orders. This is the diagonal approximation to the differential entropy of a Gaussian, where the \(1/2\) arises from the information-theoretic derivation. The resulting gradient is \(D \cdot M\Sigma\), where \(D = \text{diag}(1 / [M \Sigma M^T]_{ii})\).

Parameters:

  • M (ndarray) – The \((n, n)\) linear transformation matrix.

  • Sigmas (list of ndarray) – Covariance matrices of the 0th, 1st, or 2nd order derivatives of the source signals, as selected by params in fit_transform. Each must be \((n, n)\) and positive semi-definite.

  • compute_grad (bool, default True) – Whether to compute and return the Euclidean gradient.

Returns:

FuncResult – Scalar objective f and \((n, n)\) gradient grad (\(D \cdot M\Sigma\), summed over all \(\Sigma\)).

static right_barrier(M, S, mu, compute_grad=True)[source][source]#

Log-barrier enforcing the non-negativity constraint \(MS > 0\).

Computes:

\[h_R(M) = -\mu \sum_{i,j} \log\left([MS]_{ij} + \delta\right)\]

The barrier approaches \(+\infty\) as any element of \(MS\) approaches \(-\delta\), repelling the optimizer from the constraint boundary and ensuring the transformed source estimates remain non-negative. Returns \(f = \infty\) if the current \(M\) is already infeasible.

Parameters:

  • M (ndarray) – The \((n, n)\) transformation matrix.

  • S (ndarray) – The \((n, n_S)\) constraint matrix (convex hull vertices of the source estimates).

  • mu (float) – Barrier strength. Reduced each outer iteration via BARRIER_COOLING_RATE.

  • compute_grad (bool, default True) – Whether to compute the Euclidean gradient \(-\mu \cdot W S^T\) where \(W_{ij} = 1/([MS]_{ij} + \delta)\).

Returns:

FuncResult – Scalar objective f and \((n, n)\) gradient grad. Returns f=np.inf if any element of \(MS\) violates the constraint boundary \(-\delta\).

static left_barrier(inv_M, C, mu, compute_grad=True)[source][source]#

Log-barrier enforcing the non-negativity constraint \(M^{-T}C > 0\).

Computes:

\[h_L(M) = -\mu \sum_{i,j} \log\left([M^{-T}C]_{ij} + \delta\right)\]

This is the dual constraint to \(MS > 0\): it ensures that the columns of \(C\), when mapped by the inverse transformation \(M^{-T}\), remain non-negative. Returns \(f = \infty\) if the current \(M\) is already infeasible.

Parameters:

  • inv_M (ndarray) – The \((n, n)\) inverse of the transformation matrix \(M\).

  • C (ndarray) – The \((n, n_C)\) constraint matrix (convex hull vertices of the mixing matrix columns).

  • mu (float) – Barrier strength. Reduced each outer iteration via BARRIER_COOLING_RATE.

  • compute_grad (bool, default True) – Whether to compute the Euclidean gradient with respect to \(M\), derived via \(\partial M^{-1}/\partial M \cdot dM = -M^{-1} dM\, M^{-1}\):

    \[\frac{\partial h_L}{\partial M} = \mu \left(M^{-T}C\right) V^T M^{-T}\]

    where \(V_{ij} = 1 / ([M^{-T}C]_{ij} + \delta)\).

Returns:

FuncResult – Scalar objective f and \((n, n)\) gradient grad. Returns f=np.inf if any element of \(M^{-T}C\) violates the constraint boundary \(-\delta\).

static sparse_norm(M, S_sums, S_gram, lam, n_samples, sparsity_gate_threshold=0.5, compute_grad=True)[source][source]#

‘Safe-Plateau’ sparsity regularizer based on a gated Hoyer density.

For each row \(c\) of \(MS\), computes the Hoyer normalized density:

\[d_c = \frac{\|MS_c\|_1 / \|MS_c\|_2 - 1}{\sqrt{N} - 1} \in [0, 1]\]

where \(d_c = 0\) is maximally sparse (one nonzero) and \(d_c = 1\) is maximally dense (uniform). A negative softplus gate then rewards sparse rows while protecting dense ones:

\[f_s(M) = -\frac{\lambda}{k} \sum_c \log\left(1 + e^{k(\beta - d_c)}\right)\]

When \(d_c \ll \beta\) the gate is open and the objective is a large negative number, rewarding the optimizer for preserving sparse (peaky) rows. When \(d_c \gg \beta\) the gate saturates and the term vanishes, leaving dense rows (e.g. sine waves) governed solely by the decorrelation objective.

Parameters:

  • M (ndarray) – The \((n, n)\) transformation matrix.

  • S_sums (ndarray) – Row sums of the source matrix: \(S \mathbf{1} / N\), length \(n\). Used to efficiently compute \(\|MS\|_1\) without forming \(MS\).

  • S_gram (ndarray) – Normalised Gram matrix \(SS^T / N\), shape \((n, n)\). Used to efficiently compute \(\|MS\|_2\) without forming \(MS\).

  • lam (float) – Regularization strength. Set to 0 to disable entirely.

  • n_samples (int) – Number of columns in \(S\), used to normalize the Hoyer density.

  • sparsity_gate_threshold (float, default 0.5) – Midpoint \(\beta\) of the sigmoid gate. Rows with density below this value are penalized; rows above it are protected.

  • compute_grad (bool, default True) – Whether to compute the gradient with respect to \(M\).

Returns:

FuncResult – Scalar objective f and \((n, n)\) gradient grad. Returns f=0, grad=0 if lam <= 0.

static f(M, inv_M, Sigmas, C, S, mu, S_sums, S_gram, lam, n_samples, sparsity_gate_threshold=0.5, compute_grad=True)[source][source]#

Total objective and its projection onto the tangent space of \(SL(n)\).

Computes:

\[f(M) = f_{\text{main}}(M) + h_R(M) + h_L(M) + f_s(M)\]

When compute_grad=True, the summed Euclidean gradient \(\nabla f\) is projected onto the tangent space by removing the component that would change \(\det(M)\):

\[Z = \nabla f - \frac{\operatorname{Tr}(M^{-1} \nabla f)}{n} \cdot M\]

This is derived by solving \(\operatorname{Tr}(M^{-1} Z) = 0\) with the ansatz \(Z = \nabla f - cM\), which gives \(c = \operatorname{Tr}(M^{-1} \nabla f) / \operatorname{Tr}(I_n) = \operatorname{Tr}(M^{-1} \nabla f) / n\).

Parameters:

  • M (ndarray) – Current \((n, n)\) transformation matrix.

  • inv_M (ndarray) – Inverse of \(M\), shape \((n, n)\).

  • Sigmas (list of ndarray) – Covariance matrices of the source signals and their derivatives, each of shape \((n, n)\).

  • C (ndarray) – \((n, n_C)\) left constraint matrix (convex hull vertices).

  • S (ndarray) – \((n, n_S)\) right constraint matrix (convex hull vertices).

  • mu (float) – Current barrier strength.

  • S_sums (ndarray) – Row sums of the source matrix, length \(n\).

  • S_gram (ndarray) – Normalised Gram matrix \(SS^T / N\), shape \((n, n)\).

  • lam (float) – Sparsity regularization strength.

  • n_samples (int) – Number of columns in \(S\).

  • sparsity_gate_threshold (float, default 0.5) – Passed through to sparse_norm as the sigmoid gate midpoint \(\beta\).

  • compute_grad (bool, default True) – Whether to compute the projected tangent gradient \(Z\).

Returns:

FuncResult – Scalar objective f and projected tangent gradient grad \(Z\).

static optimize_step(M, inv_M, Sigmas, C, S, mu, S_sums, S_gram, lam, n_samples, sparsity_gate_threshold, initial_lr, max_line_search_iters)[source][source]#

Single Riemannian descent step via two-phase backtracking line search.

Phase 1 — Linearized backtracking: Uses the first-order Taylor approximation of the matrix inverse to cheaply find a step size \(\alpha\) satisfying the Armijo sufficient decrease condition:

\[(M - \alpha Z)^{-1} \approx M^{-1} + \alpha M^{-1} Z M^{-1}\]

Phase 2 — Manifold retraction: Confirms the step using the exact matrix exponential retraction, starting from the \(\alpha\) found in Phase 1 and continuing to backtrack if needed:

\[M_{\text{new}} = M \exp(-\alpha \Omega), \quad M_{\text{new}}^{-1} = \exp(\alpha \Omega) M^{-1}\]

where \(\Omega = M^{-1} Z\) is the descent direction in the Lie algebra.

Parameters:

  • M (ndarray) – Current \((n, n)\) transformation matrix.

  • inv_M (ndarray) – Inverse of \(M\), shape \((n, n)\).

  • Sigmas (list of ndarray) – Covariance matrices of the source signals and their derivatives, each of shape \((n, n)\).

  • C (ndarray) – \((n, n_C)\) left constraint matrix (convex hull vertices).

  • S (ndarray) – \((n, n_S)\) right constraint matrix (convex hull vertices).

  • mu (float) – Current barrier strength.

  • S_sums (ndarray) – Row sums of the source matrix, length \(n\).

  • S_gram (ndarray) – Normalised Gram matrix \(SS^T / N\), shape \((n, n)\).

  • lam (float) – Sparsity regularization strength.

  • n_samples (int) – Number of columns in \(S\).

  • sparsity_gate_threshold (float) – Sigmoid gate midpoint \(\beta\) passed through to sparse_norm.

  • initial_lr (float) – Starting step size \(\alpha\) for backtracking.

  • max_line_search_iters (int) – Maximum number of backtracking steps in each phase before declaring failure.

Returns:

  • success (bool) – True if a descent step satisfying the Armijo condition was found.

  • M_new (ndarray) – Updated transformation matrix (unchanged if success=False).

  • inv_M_new (ndarray) – Inverse of M_new (unchanged if success=False).

static normalize(C, S)[source][source]#

Rescales \(C\) and \(S\) so that their row variances are balanced across the left and right barrier terms, and both matrices have unit standard deviation.

Computes two diagonal scaling matrices \(\Lambda_C\) and \(\Lambda_S\) such that:

\[C_{\text{norm}} = \Lambda_C \cdot C, \quad S_{\text{norm}} = \Lambda_S \cdot S\]

The scaling has two components applied sequentially:

1. Barrier balancing: \(\lambda_i = (\text{Var}(C_i) / \text{Var}(S_i))^{1/4}\) distributes the variance ratio evenly between \(C\) and \(S\) in log-space, equalizing barrier gradient magnitudes.

2. Std normalization: both matrices are divided by their global standard deviation so typical entry magnitudes are \(O(1)\), making BARRIER_DELTA meaningful across datasets of different scales.

The scaling matrices allow the transformation to be inverted exactly:

\[C = \Lambda_C^{-1} C_{\text{norm}}, \quad S = \Lambda_S^{-1} S_{\text{norm}}\]
Parameters:

  • C (ndarray) – \((n, n_C)\) left constraint matrix.

  • S (ndarray) – \((n, n_S)\) right constraint matrix.

Returns:

  • C_norm (ndarray) – Normalized version of \(C\), shape \((n, n_C)\).

  • S_norm (ndarray) – Normalized version of \(S\), shape \((n, n_S)\).

  • Lambda_C (ndarray) – \((n, n)\) diagonal scaling matrix for \(C\).

  • Lambda_S (ndarray) – \((n, n)\) diagonal scaling matrix for \(S\).

get_covariances(S, params)[source][source]#

Covariance matrices of \(S\) and its filtered temporal derivatives.

For each active flag in params, computes the \((n, n)\) covariance matrix of the corresponding derivative of \(S\). All orders are computed on the band-limited signal via unsupervised Parks-McClellan FIR filters tuned by minimizing the MSRAC of the rejected band, ensuring consistent frequency content across all covariance matrices.

If the signal is too short to apply filtering safely, all orders fall back to using the raw (unfiltered) signal.

Parameters:

  • S (ndarray) – \((n, n_{\text{samples}})\) source signal matrix, one row per channel.

  • params (tuple) – Flags selecting which derivative orders to include: (use_0th, use_1st, use_2nd). At least one must be True. Multiple True flags produce multiple covariance matrices, all included in the returned list.

Returns:

list of ndarray – Covariance matrices of shape \((n, n)\), one per active flag in params, in order of derivative order.

Warns:

UserWarning – If \(n_{\text{samples}} < 2m + \text{max_{\text{lag}}} + 1\), the signal is too short to filter safely. All derivative orders fall back to raw (unfiltered) covariances.

prune(data, gamma=0.01)[source][source]#

Removes low-magnitude points clustered near the origin.

Two thresholds are computed and the minimum is taken as the effective cutoff, protecting against outliers inflating the max-based threshold and against dense origin clusters inflating the percentile-based one:

  • Percentile threshold: the \(\gamma\)-percentile of point magnitudes.

  • Max threshold: \(\gamma \times \max(\|x\|)\).

Points with magnitude below the effective threshold are removed. If pruning would leave fewer than \(d + 1\) points (the minimum for a non-degenerate convex hull in \(d\) dimensions), the original data is returned unchanged.

Parameters:

  • data (ndarray) – \((d, N)\) data matrix.

  • gamma (float, default 0.01) – Controls the pruning threshold as a fraction of the data’s magnitude range. Larger values prune more aggressively.

Returns:

ndarray – Pruned data matrix of shape \((d, N')\) where \(N' \leq N\).

extract_boundary(data)[source][source]#

Extracts the outer boundary points of the dataset.

Uses one of two methods depending on dimensionality and dataset size:

Tier 1 — Exact Convex Hull (\(d \leq\) CONVEX_HULL_MAX_DIM, \(N \leq\) CONVEX_HULL_MAX_SAMPLES): computes the exact convex hull via QHull and returns its vertices. Falls back to Tier 2 if QHull fails (e.g. perfectly collinear data). These thresholds reflect empirically observed performance limits of the QHull algorithm.

Tier 2 — Support Function Approximation (high-dimensional or large \(N\)): evaluates the support function of the dataset along \(2d\) axis-aligned basis directions and \(d \times \texttt{NUM_PROBES_PER_D}\) random unit directions, returning the unique set of extreme points found.

Reference#

Sartipizadeh, H., & Suryanarayanan, S. (2016). “Computing the Approximate Convex Hull in High Dimensions.” IEEE Access.

Parameters:

data (ndarray) – \((d, N)\) data matrix of boundary candidates.

returns:

ndarray – \((d, N')\) matrix of boundary points where \(N' \leq N\). Returns data unchanged if \(N < 3\).

fit_transform(C, S)[source][source]#

Orchestrates the barrier method to find the optimal transformation \(M\).

Follows an interior point central path: starting from a large \(\mu\), the inner loop minimizes \(f(M)\) for fixed \(\mu\), then \(\mu\) is cooled by BARRIER_COOLING_RATE and the process repeats until the duality gap \(n_{\text{constraints}} \cdot \mu\) falls below tol.

\(M\) is optimized in \(SL(n)\) by projecting gradients onto the tangent space, keeping \(\det(M)\) stable throughout.

Parameters:

  • C (ndarray) – \((n, n_C)\) left constraint matrix. All elements must be non-negative.

  • S (ndarray) – \((n, n_S)\) right constraint (source) matrix. All elements must be non-negative.

Returns:

MIOptimizerResult – Contains the optimized matrix x, convergence info success and message, final objective fun, final gradient jac, iteration counts nit and nit_outer, and the transformed constraint matrices inv_MT_C and MS for verification.
